analysis:
Examined scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py head lines 1-874. This is an offline CI workflow self-test, not provider runtime code; it asserts on the shape of workflow YAML.

Changed behavior visible in this batch:
- Head lines 393-396 add an assertion that the provider-test-gate record step also invokes `ci-tested-tree.py tree-name --tree "$TREE" --components "$RAN"`.
- The same lines require a new "Upload the tree record" step to share the condition `inputs.skip != 'true' && (inputs.provider == 'true' || inputs.cluster == 'true')`.
- Per the patch excerpt (head ~886-898, outside this batch's text), build jobs now run only when `inputs.<lane> == 'true'`. A push of an already-tested tree no longer builds the changed components to refresh caches.

Why no regression was identified:
- Neither change affects provider runtime behavior or any threat-model asset: A-001..A-020, TB-002/003/007/009/011-014, T-041 cache crypto.
- They also do not affect release signing or qualification (A-011/A-017, T-054).
- The tests still pin the signing-rule checks, Date-comparison checks and signature-certificate pin checks to run on every run (head 356-374).
- The .git cache validation and the Actions-cache gating remain asserted (head 152-196).
- Removing cache-refresh builds on tested-tree pushes reduces work. It does not weaken a gate: the record and upload only occur when tests ran.

Integration questions:
- Can the tested-tree record mechanism (scripts/ci-tested-tree.py tree-name, provider-plan.yml) let a tree skip tests based on a record forged or poisoned through PR artifacts or caches?
- In particular, can a pull-request run upload a tree record that a later push trusts in order to skip build/test?
- That logic is not in the supplied evidence, so it remains a CI supply-chain question rather than a finding. It is relevant to release integrity only indirectly, since signing happens on dev/master pushes.
